---
name: porting-symbols
description: "How a scheduled C symbol is reimplemented in safe Rust, porting's symbol route: functions and their exports, globals, function pointers, static inline functions and macros, each with its later stages. Read before porting any symbol, and when reviewing ports."
---

# Porting symbols

How a scheduled C symbol is reimplemented in safe Rust: the symbol route, which follows
[`porting`](../SKILL.md)'s FFI boundary section and starts from
[`binding-symbols`](../../binding/symbols/SKILL.md)'s; the types it reaches are
[`porting-types`](../types/SKILL.md)'s.

A ported symbol's implementation is translated to safe, idiomatic Rust with its observable
behaviour preserved.

## 1. Functions

A ported function takes the safe API [`binding-symbols`](../../binding/symbols/SKILL.md)'s Functions
section gives a function, or keeps its wrapper's, as [`porting`](../SKILL.md)'s FFI boundary section describes.

A function no wrapper gives an API yet, whose body only reads or writes one member, or only
returns a value an existing item of its own module's safe API already gives, is ported as
that item, so that the port writes no second API: the accessor or method carries the
function's `Replaces` anchor and alias beside its own. Its export, where remaining C calls
it, is written in the module's gateway, over that item.

A function that remaining C calls or takes the address of is exported, as
[`porting`](../SKILL.md)'s FFI boundary section describes. Its gateway undoes what the safe API converted,
so that its C callers see what the C function did: it rebuilds the safe arguments from the
C ones, writes the out-parameters and buffers through the pointers C passed, and reports a
failure through the function's C error convention, its return and the error state the C
function set, `errno` included, which the Rust behind it never sets. A panic is caught at
the gateway and reported as a failure, or aborts where the function cannot fail: none
unwinds into C. The gateway checks each export against the raw binding of the C declaration
it replaces, as [`testing-gates`](../../../verification/testing/gates/SKILL.md)' Regressions
section asks, in a constant the compiler evaluates, `const _: () = { let _ = [sys::<name>,
<name>]; };`, whose two function items coerce to one function-pointer type only where their
signatures agree; the binding is allowlisted for it where the bindings lack it. A variadic function's export cannot be defined on stable Rust, so a shim
keeps its C signature, as [`bindgen`](../../bindgen/SKILL.md)'s shims are compiled, and calls
a fixed-arity export with the arguments it formats or unpacks. Its later stage, `port/unexport`, removes the
export, with the raw binding and the allowlist entry that reach it and its declaration in its
header, once no remaining C references it. C that only a configuration the target is built
without compiles, such as another platform's, is no remaining C: like a test case
configured out, as [`porting-workflow`](../../../workflows/porting-workflow/SKILL.md)'s Tests
follow their modules section describes, it holds no export back, and a build under that
configuration meets the function undeclared where it calls it.

A lifecycle routine's port reimplements it behind the policy its type's port or wrap
wrote, which it repoints at the Rust routine, and writes no API of its own, as `binding-types`'
Lifecycle section has the symbol route skip what a type batch emitted. The last of its
type's own module's memory users to be ported moves its storage to Rust's allocator,
unless C of other modules still allocates or frees it raw, which leaves that move to its
`port/memory`.

## 2. Globals

A ported global takes the safe API [`binding-symbols`](../../binding/symbols/SKILL.md)'s
Globals section gives a global, or keeps its wrapper's. Rust holds its storage from its
port, beside its module's C, which keeps its own copy until the switch; from then on
the Rust's is the only one. A global that remaining C accesses
is exported, as a function is, and keeps the C layout and the synchronization protocol
those accesses rely on while it is. Its later stage, `port/unexport`, removes the export, as
a function's does, and its storage then takes a native form, as state moved out of C does.
A thread-local one cannot be defined for C on stable Rust, so a shim keeps its C definition,
as [`bindgen`](../../bindgen/SKILL.md)'s shims are compiled, until that stage. A global no
remaining C accesses is native from its port.

## 3. Function pointers

A ported function pointer keeps the safe callable type
[`binding-symbols`](../../binding/symbols/SKILL.md)'s Function pointers section gives it, which is its API from its port: its Rust consumers, and
the ported code that calls it, use that type alone. While remaining C calls a function
pointer of its type or supplies one, its C form stays beneath it: the function-pointer type
of its raw binding, the trampolines through which a Rust closure reaches the C that calls
it, and the `unsafe` constructor through which a C function reaches Rust, passed to an
export, whose gateway builds the C variant from the function and the context it receives,
or stored where C wrote it. Its later stage, `port/unexport`, removes that C form, with the
raw binding and the allowlist entry that reach it, once no remaining C references it, as
[`scheduling`](../../../planning/scheduling/SKILL.md)'s Later stages section times it. A
function pointer no remaining C calls or supplies by its port is native in its
implementation too: its closure or trait alone.
A function pointer on the target's public API keeps its closure or trait through its
`port/unexport`, even when Rust alone implements it, so that the deferred public C API, as
[`conventions`](../../conventions/SKILL.md)'s Exports section describes, can let C
implement it again.

## 4. Static inline functions

A `static inline` function a header defines is internal API of the module the
decomposition gives it, and is ported as its other functions are. Its C callers expand its
body in their own TUs, so an export alone does not reach them: at the module's
switch, the header's definition is replaced by its prototype, and the remaining C
calls the Rust module's export, under the function's bare name, where it inlined the body.
<!-- TODO: cross-language LTO (`-Clinker-plugin-lto`, with a clang whose LLVM matches
rustc's) would inline the export back into its C callers. -->

name: porting
description: "How a scheduled C item is reimplemented in safe Rust: its native API, its later stages, the FFI boundary and its exports, and the routes porting-types and porting-symbols give types and symbols. Read before porting any item, and when reviewing ports."
---

# Porting

How a scheduled C item is reimplemented in safe Rust. A port starts from the item's
analysis, as [`analysis`](../analysis/SKILL.md) describes, and keeps C interoperability
and observable behaviour for as long as C consumes the item. A type takes the type route,
for structs, unions, enums and typedefs, as [`porting-types`](types/SKILL.md) describes; a
symbol the symbol route, for functions, globals, function pointers, static inline functions
and macros, as [`porting-symbols`](symbols/SKILL.md) describes.

A port gives an item its native safe API at once, and that API does not change after it.
An item the remaining C still uses keeps a C form behind it, its C layout, its storage in
C's allocator, its export or its integer values, so that the C keeps working while its
Rust consumers stay agnostic of which form implements it. The later stages its kind
describes below migrate that form to Rust, part by part, once the switches that free
it have landed, as [`scheduling`](../../planning/scheduling/SKILL.md)'s Later stages
section schedules them. An item no C uses is native in its API and its implementation from
its port.

A later stage changes the item and the code inside the crate that reaches its C form, in
its module's unsafe regions, as the [conventions](../conventions/SKILL.md)' Unsafe regions
section describes, never the safe API its consumers use, and keeps the item's tests
passing. A stage that moves state out of C, a lock or a handle a type held in its C layout,
or memory C's allocator held, moves its uses onto the standard library where
[`binding`](../binding/SKILL.md)'s Safe boundary section lets it.

## 1. FFI boundary

`binding`'s Safe boundary section applies to a port unchanged. When a wrapper of the item
already exists, because a module that ran before needed it, the port keeps that wrapper's
safe API and replaces only what is behind it, so that its consumers do not change, as do
its later stages. A standard-library operation is used directly when it is equivalent and
no C-interoperability requirement remains, an out-of-tree library's entity included, as
`binding`'s Safe boundary section describes.

While C consumers remain, a ported item is re-exported to C as the
[conventions](../conventions/SKILL.md)' Exports section describes:

- The raw gateway, its module's `ffi_export` region, reconstructs safe wrappers and calls
  the native function.
- The gateway is compiled only under its module's export feature, which stays off until
  the module switches, so that the exports never collide with the C they replace.
- At the switch, the Rust static library is linked in place of the TU through the actual
  build system, without assuming link mechanics, and the TU is deleted, as
  [`porting-workflow`](../../workflows/porting-workflow/SKILL.md)'s Builds section describes.

### 1.2 Tests follow their modules

Each module carries the C tests tied to it, those whose subject it is, as
[`decomposition`](../../planning/decomposition/SKILL.md)'s Bundling section describes.
They assert the C contract, which a safe Rust implementation may change. Those that reach
the module's internals run while it is C and leave with it at its switch. Those that
use only its public API stay, and check its exports, which keep that contract for the C
that calls them, until their `port/unexport` carries them over, as the
[conventions](../../rust/conventions/SKILL.md)' Exports section describes. The tests its
port batches write mirror their regression cases, as
[`testing`](../../verification/testing/SKILL.md)'s C tests carried over section describes. A
test's access to a module's internals is a use within that module, so it never keeps a type
wrapped.

A C test that only calls a module, to set up or tear down its fixtures, is not tied to it:
once the module has switched, the test reaches it through its exports, so that it checks
its own subject with the ported Rust under it, as part of the integration regression gate. A
test never keeps an export the remaining C no longer needs: the export's `port/unexport`
carries over the test cases that still reference it, as
[`scheduling`](../../planning/scheduling/SKILL.md)'s Later stages section describes.

A test whose subject is several modules is tied to each of them, and leaves at the first
point at which it would leave as a test of one of them alone. Each ported module's own
tests cover it from then on.

A test case whose body the configured build compiles empty, under a configuration the
target is built without, such as `GIT_WIN32`, tests nothing of the target: it is out of
scope, as a configured-out translation unit is, tied to no module and holding nothing back.

### 1.3 One language per module

A module is in one language at a time. The campaign maintains C and Rust side by side, but
on disjoint modules, never the same code in both.

While the waves of a module's `wrap` and `port` items run, its C is the reference its
ports are tested against, and the target is built and linked from C alone.
Once the last of them has landed, the module switches to Rust, once, as [Builds](#3-builds)
describes: the Rust module replaces the TU in the target's link, its C is removed from the
build and from the tree, and its tests switch with it. The removal is made on the working branch; the shipping branch keeps the C until
the user approves shipping the module. From then on the module is Rust's: what it still
keeps for the remaining C, its types' C layouts and storage and its exports, its later
stages remove after the switch, as [Later stages](#4-later-stages) describes.

The headers bundled with the module stay while remaining C includes them, declaring the
module's exports, its `static inline` functions included, as
[`porting-symbols`](../../rust/porting/symbols/SKILL.md)'s Static inline functions section describes, and go with the last C
file that includes them.

The module's equivalence tests, which need the C, are retired with it, and the behaviour
they established is kept by its unit tests. Before the module's equivalence tests are
retired, each that needs no C is carried over to the module's unit tests, where what it
compares with stays after the switch, such as the constants of a header that remaining C
still includes. The raw bindings of its
exported functions and globals then reach its exports, so that a consumer's raw calls keep
working, and an allowlist entry goes with the export it reaches. Those of its functions and
globals that have no export, which only its own C referenced, are removed with their
allowlist entries at the switch.

A ported module's items therefore reach the rest of its module natively from the start:
an edge within a module needs neither a `wrap` binding nor an export, only the edges that
leave it.

## 2. Batches

A port campaign's schedule mixes both kinds of batch, as [`scheduling`](../../planning/scheduling/SKILL.md)'s
Waves and batches section describes: a selected symbol is `port` from the start, a
selected type is `wrap` while another module's unported C depends on its layout and `port`
once none does, and a dependency outside the selected migration set stays `wrap`. A type
whose layout only its own module and tests use is `port` from the start. Each batch runs
the agent its objective names, in the same waves.

## 3. Builds

A module's waves do not change the compiled target. Its `port` batches add Rust that is
built and tested on its own, against the target's C build, which still compiles the
module's C and links no Rust: there is no build switch, and no batch flips one. The
module's `ffi_export` gateway is written with its items but compiled only under its export
feature, as the [conventions](../../rust/conventions/SKILL.md)' Exports and Export features sections

link. Native Rust items carry mangled names and cannot collide with it.

The C stays until the switch: the target's other C still calls the module's symbols, which
only the exports could define, and the module's equivalence tests and its cut cycles still
run through it.

in one step, with concurrent modules as part of its branch's integration into the working
branch, as [`versioning`](../../operations/versioning/SKILL.md)'s Integration section

   describes.

   which the Rust library holds only once the export feature is deleted.
4. The gates, over those builds.

as C and as Rust, nor its Rust twice:

[`testing-gates`](../../verification/testing/gates/SKILL.md)'s Regressions section describes.
For that link, the first switch changes the fork's C build so that the remaining C's
tests and executables link the safe crate's Rust library, static or shared, in the build
system's own idiom, and each later switch takes its module's C out of that build.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Seed one fault at a time in src/libgit2/src/util/thread.rs of a scratch tree and run the
module's tests over each, by binary, with the module's export feature on, as the switch
compiles it.

    mutate.py <scratch tree> <mutants.json> <out.json> [ids...]

Each mutant is {"id", "kind", "old", "new"}: `old` must occur exactly once in the pristine
file. Each binary's thread tests run alone under a timeout; a test that fails, or a binary
that times out or aborts, catches the mutant. The equivalence tests (the `equiv` binary and
the gateway's `equiv_priv`) retire at the switch; every other test outlives the C.
"""
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import time

tree, mutants_path, out_path = sys.argv[1:4]
only = set(sys.argv[4:])
src = os.path.join(tree, "src/libgit2/src/util/thread.rs")
pristine = open(src).read()
mutants = json.load(open(mutants_path))
runner = [os.path.join(tree, "crustify/scripts/cargo-variant.sh"), "plain", "test",
          "--features", "ffi-export-src-util-thread-c"]
binaries = {"lib": ["--lib"], "unit_pub": ["--test", "unit_pub"], "ub_safe": ["--test", "ub_safe"],
            "ub_unsafe": ["--test", "ub_unsafe"], "equiv": ["--test", "equiv"]}
results = json.load(open(out_path)) if os.path.exists(out_path) else {}


def run(args, timeout):
    try:
        p = subprocess.run(args, cwd=tree, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)
        return p.returncode, p.stdout + p.stderr
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as e:
        out = (e.stdout or b"").decode(errors="replace") + (e.stderr or b"").decode(errors="replace")
        return "timeout", out


try:
    for m in mutants:
        if only and m["id"] not in only:
            continue
        if m["id"] in results and not only:
            continue
        assert pristine.count(m["old"]) == 1, (m["id"], pristine.count(m["old"]))
        open(src, "w").write(pristine.replace(m["old"], m["new"]))
        t0 = time.time()
        rc, out = run(runner + [b for v in binaries.values() for b in v] + ["--no-run"], 1800)
        r = {"kind": m["kind"], "desc": m.get("desc", ""), "build": rc}
        if rc != 0:
            r["build_log"] = out[-3000:]
        else:
            for name, sel in binaries.items():
                brc, bout = run(runner + sel + ["--", "util::thread"], 240)
                failed = sorted(set(re.findall(r"^test (\S+) \.\.\. FAILED", bout, re.M)))
                passed = len(re.findall(r"^test \S+ \.\.\. ok", bout, re.M))
                r[name] = {"rc": brc, "failed": failed, "passed": passed}
                if brc != 0 and not failed:
                    r[name]["tail"] = bout[-1500:]
        r["secs"] = round(time.time() - t0)
        results[m["id"]] = r
        json.dump(results, open(out_path, "w"), indent=1)
        print(m["id"], {k: (v["rc"], len(v["failed"])) for k, v in r.items() if isinstance(v, dict)},
              r["build"], flush=True)
finally:
    open(src, "w").write(pristine)

module's tests over each, by binary, with the module's export feature on, as the switch
compiles it.

    mutate.py <scratch tree> <mutants.json> <out.json> [ids...]

Each mutant is {"id", "kind", "old", "new"}: `old` must occur exactly once in the pristine
file. Each binary's thread tests run alone under a timeout; a test that fails, or a binary
that times out or aborts, catches the mutant. The equivalence tests (the `equiv` binary and
the gateway's `equiv_priv`) retire at the switch; every other test outlives the C.
"""
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import time

tree, mutants_path, out_path = sys.argv[1:4]
only = set(sys.argv[4:])
src = os.path.join(tree, "src/libgit2/src/util/thread.rs")
pristine = open(src).read()
mutants = json.load(open(mutants_path))
runner = [os.path.join(tree, "crustify/scripts/cargo-variant.sh"), "plain", "test",
          "--features", "ffi-export-src-util-thread-c"]
binaries = {"lib": ["--lib"], "unit_pub": ["--test", "unit_pub"], "ub_safe": ["--test", "ub_safe"],
            "ub_unsafe": ["--test", "ub_unsafe"], "equiv": ["--test", "equiv"]}
results = json.load(open(out_path)) if os.path.exists(out_path) else {}


def run(args, timeout):
    try:
        p = subprocess.run(args, cwd=tree, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)
        return p.returncode, p.stdout + p.stderr
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as e:
        out = (e.stdout or b"").decode(errors="replace") + (e.stderr or b"").decode(errors="replace")
        return "timeout", out


try:
    for m in mutants:
        if only and m["id"] not in only:
            continue
        if m["id"] in results and not only:
            continue
        assert pristine.count(m["old"]) == 1, (m["id"], pristine.count(m["old"]))
        open(src, "w").write(pristine.replace(m["old"], m["new"]))
        t0 = time.time()
        rc, out = run(runner + [b for v in binaries.values() for b in v] + ["--no-run"], 1800)
        r = {"kind": m["kind"], "desc": m.get("desc", ""), "build": rc}
        if rc != 0:
            r["build_log"] = out[-3000:]
        else:
            for name, sel in binaries.items():
                brc, bout = run(runner + sel + ["--", "util::thread"], 240)
                failed = sorted(set(re.findall(r"^test (\S+) \.\.\. FAILED", bout, re.M)))
                passed = len(re.findall(r"^test \S+ \.\.\. ok", bout, re.M))
                r[name] = {"rc": brc, "failed": failed, "passed": passed}
                if brc != 0 and not failed:
                    r[name]["tail"] = bout[-1500:]
        r["secs"] = round(time.time() - t0)
        results[m["id"]] = r
        json.dump(results, open(out_path, "w"), indent=1)
        print(m["id"], {k: (v["rc"], len(v["failed"])) for k, v in r.items() if isinstance(v, dict)},
              r["build"], flush=True)
finally:
    open(src, "w").write(pristine)

content.content:
## 4. Landing

A batch lands its commits on the integration branch it was given, which is never checked
out. Before committing, the diff is checked to contain no unrelated work. A commit carries
no trailer but the co-author trailers of the campaign's [identity](#6-identity), and its
subject says what it does and which run made it. A batch's names its module's file and its
objective and ends with its run's id, as `refs.c: wrap 12 items (wave-3/batch-1/run-2)`,
and its body lists the items it translated by their anchors' paths, as
`fn::git_reference_lookup`, one per line; a review batch's two commits name what they file
and what they fix the same way, and a planner run's subject ends with its run's id. A
progress commit is `progress: wave-<index>`, and an integration's merge, in the campaign's
repository and on the fork's `main`, `integrate <module>`, the module written as
[`modules-schema`](../../artifacts/modules-schema/SKILL.md) writes it.

The landing operation is a local push of the batch's tip to the integration branch through
the repository's Git common directory, which accepts only a fast-forward. A direct ref
update is no substitute: its compare-and-swap form makes the update atomic, but does not
enforce that the new commit descends from the expected old commit.

### 4.1 The landing lock

An integration branch is landed on by one batch at a time, under its landing lock: an
exclusive `flock` on a file in the Git common directory, named after the branch with its
`refs/heads/` prefix dropped, so that every worktree of the repository sees the same lock:

```text
$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/crustify/landing/<integration branch>.lock
```

A batch whose validated work is committed on its own branch takes the lock and holds it
until its landing has succeeded:

1. it acquires the lock, waiting while another batch holds it;
2. it rebases only its own branch onto the current integration branch, once: nothing else
   lands while it holds the lock;
3. it resolves any conflict the rebase raises and runs again, on the rebased tree, the
   gates that could catch a regression of the integration, as
   [`testing-gates`](../../verification/testing/gates/SKILL.md)'s Regressions section describes, fixing what fails;
4. it pushes the fast-forward, which nothing can reject; and
5. it releases the lock.

A conflict or a failing gate is resolved under the lock rather than after releasing it, so
that the branch cannot move again in between and no batch rebases twice.

The waiter blocks in `flock` itself, so the kernel wakes it the moment the lock is released,
and nothing polls. Once it holds the lock, it hands the locked descriptor to a process of
its own, detached from the shell that started it and bound to the lifetime of the agent's
CLI: a `flock` lock belongs to the open file, so that process keeps it after the command
that took it exits, until that CLI ends, however it ends, and the kernel releases it. The
holder records itself beside the lock, in `<integration branch>.lock.holder`, as its own pid
and the CLI's. A waiter bounds each wait, to stay within the time a single command may run,
and waits again when it expires. For example, with `$CLI_PID` the agent CLI's pid, found by
walking up the shell's parent processes:
<!-- TODO: this procedure must run exactly so: it belongs in a script beside this skill,
documented by its `--help`, as `authoring` describes. -->

```bash
lock="$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/crustify/landing/<integration branch>.lock"
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$lock")"
# wait in the kernel, up to 10 minutes per command; then hand the lock to a detached holder
sh -c '
  exec 9>"$1"
  flock -w 600 9 || exit 1
  setsid sh -c "echo \"\$\$ $2\" > \"$1.holder\"; exec tail --pid=$2 -f /dev/null" 9>&9 &
' sh "$lock" "$CLI_PID"
# release, once the push has succeeded
holder=$(cut -d' ' -f1 "$lock.holder"); rm -f "$lock.holder"; kill "$holder"
```

The holder file is removed before the holder is ended, while the lock is still held, so
that a release never removes the next holder's record.

The lock has no timeout: the regression gates it covers vary in length. A holder that has
stopped making progress keeps it until its agent is ended. That releases it where the
agent ran in a CLI of its own. An agent that shared its CLI with others leaves its holder
running: the holder is then ended as a release ends it, by the pid its record names, the
record removed first. The batch is then run again, as any failed batch is.

### 4.2 Commits

Every landing is a fast-forward, so an integration branch is linear, and each batch's
commits are one unbroken run of it, ending at its branch's tip and starting after the wave
base or the tip of the batch that landed before it: the commits its branch reaches and
neither the wave base nor the wave's other landed batches reach, oldest first, which
become the batch's `commits` in `schedule.json`.

The integration branch is never reset, force-updated or moved backward, and nothing is
pushed to a remote. The worktree stays after landing, until it is purged as [Lifecycle](#5-lifecycle)
describes.

A batch lands its commits on the integration branch it was given, which is never checked
out. Before committing, the diff is checked to contain no unrelated work. A commit carries
no trailer but the co-author trailers of the campaign's [identity](#6-identity), and its
subject says what it does and which run made it. A batch's names its module's file and its
objective and ends with its run's id, as `refs.c: wrap 12 items (wave-3/batch-1/run-2)`,
and its body lists the items it translated by their anchors' paths, as
`fn::git_reference_lookup`, one per line; a review batch's two commits name what they file
and what they fix the same way, and a planner run's subject ends with its run's id. A
progress commit is `progress: wave-<index>`, and an integration's merge, in the campaign's
repository and on the fork's `main`, `integrate <module>`, the module written as
[`modules-schema`](../../artifacts/modules-schema/SKILL.md) writes it.

The landing operation is a local push of the batch's tip to the integration branch through
the repository's Git common directory, which accepts only a fast-forward. A direct ref
update is no substitute: its compare-and-swap form makes the update atomic, but does not
enforce that the new commit descends from the expected old commit.

### 4.1 The landing lock

An integration branch is landed on by one batch at a time, under its landing lock: an
exclusive `flock` on a file in the Git common directory, named after the branch with its
`refs/heads/` prefix dropped, so that every worktree of the repository sees the same lock:

```text
$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/crustify/landing/<integration branch>.lock
```

A batch whose validated work is committed on its own branch takes the lock and holds it
until its landing has succeeded:

1. it acquires the lock, waiting while another batch holds it;
2. it rebases only its own branch onto the current integration branch, once: nothing else
   lands while it holds the lock;
3. it resolves any conflict the rebase raises and runs again, on the rebased tree, the
   gates that could catch a regression of the integration, as
   [`testing-gates`](../../verification/testing/gates/SKILL.md)'s Regressions section describes, fixing what fails;
4. it pushes the fast-forward, which nothing can reject; and
5. it releases the lock.

A conflict or a failing gate is resolved under the lock rather than after releasing it, so
that the branch cannot move again in between and no batch rebases twice.

The waiter blocks in `flock` itself, so the kernel wakes it the moment the lock is released,
and nothing polls. Once it holds the lock, it hands the locked descriptor to a process of
its own, detached from the shell that started it and bound to the lifetime of the agent's
CLI: a `flock` lock belongs to the open file, so that process keeps it after the command
that took it exits, until that CLI ends, however it ends, and the kernel releases it. The
holder records itself beside the lock, in `<integration branch>.lock.holder`, as its own pid
and the CLI's. A waiter bounds each wait, to stay within the time a single command may run,
and waits again when it expires. For example, with `$CLI_PID` the agent CLI's pid, found by
walking up the shell's parent processes:
<!-- TODO: this procedure must run exactly so: it belongs in a script beside this skill,
documented by its `--help`, as `authoring` describes. -->

```bash
lock="$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/crustify/landing/<integration branch>.lock"
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$lock")"
# wait in the kernel, up to 10 minutes per command; then hand the lock to a detached holder
sh -c '
  exec 9>"$1"
  flock -w 600 9 || exit 1
  setsid sh -c "echo \"\$\$ $2\" > \"$1.holder\"; exec tail --pid=$2 -f /dev/null" 9>&9 &
' sh "$lock" "$CLI_PID"
# release, once the push has succeeded
holder=$(cut -d' ' -f1 "$lock.holder"); rm -f "$lock.holder"; kill "$holder"
```

The holder file is removed before the holder is ended, while the lock is still held, so
that a release never removes the next holder's record.

The lock has no timeout: the regression gates it covers vary in length. A holder that has
stopped making progress keeps it until its agent is ended. That releases it where the
agent ran in a CLI of its own. An agent that shared its CLI with others leaves its holder
running: the holder is then ended as a release ends it, by the pid its record names, the
record removed first. The batch is then run again, as any failed batch is.

The integration branch is never reset, force-updated or moved backward, and nothing is
pushed to a remote. The worktree stays after landing, until it is purged as [Lifecycle](#5-lifecycle)

content.content:
## 4. Proposals

A proposal is filed in the campaign's repository under `crustify/evolution/<slug>/`, as its
`PROPOSAL.md`. It states:

- the signal and its evidence, with the runs, findings and commits it cites;
- the goal it serves, by name, and the fitness measure of that goal it expects to move;
- its destination;
- the change, or the patch;
- how it was validated;
- the row the record takes when the change lands, as [`evolution-record`](record/SKILL.md) describes;
- its review's verdict; and
- its status: `open`; `deferred`, with what it waits for; `landed`, with the commit it
  landed as; `declined`, with why; or `superseded`, with the proposal that replaces it.

The campaign keeps an index of its proposals, `crustify/evolution/INDEX.md`, one row per
proposal: its slug, its signal in a line, its status, the runs that met the signal, and the
row of the record it matches, if any. The index has one writer per campaign, so that two
runs never write a row at once. It is written as each batch's proposals land, and holds
every proposal of the campaign before a wave launches.

A signal is filed once while its proposal waits. Before a run files a proposal, it reads the
index, in its worktree, and the record, in Crustify's checkout. Campaigns that share a
component's working branch, as a side campaign does with its parent, read each other's index
too:

- where the index holds its signal in a proposal that is `open` or `deferred`, the run files
  nothing new. When that proposal is in the run's own repository, the run adds its evidence
  to it, as an occurrence; otherwise, the run reports the occurrence in its final message,
  and the index's writer records it;
- otherwise, where its signal meets the recurrence signal of a row of the record, the change
  that landed did not hold: the run files a new proposal that cites the row, as
  [`evolution-record`](record/SKILL.md)'s Record section describes; and
- otherwise, the run files the proposal.

A lesson is not filed as a proposal: `LESSONS.md` records it. A defect in a tool found
while reviewing is a proposal, not a finding on the reviewed code, and is filed with its
reproducer.

## 5. Lessons

The campaign's lessons sit in `crustify/LESSONS.md`, read by every run of the campaign
before its first step. Each lesson is one entry, under a heading that is its id: a short
slug no other lesson of the file has. An entry holds a status, one rule, the evidence the
rule rests on, and, on a line of its own, its scope: the modules, items or stages it holds
for.

A lesson steers every later run, as a rule of the spec does, so it is reviewed:

- A new or changed lesson is `provisional`. The first review batch whose worklist holds the
  commit that added or changed it reads it, against its evidence, its scope and the
  generality test of [Destinations](#3-destinations). A lesson no worklist holds, such as
  one a wave's last review batch adds, is read by the next review batch the campaign
  launches.
- The review batch that reads a lesson marks it `held` in its landing. A lesson it judges
  wrong, or one that belongs in the spec, is a finding of that batch: under `fix`, the
  batch corrects the entry, retires it, or files the proposal it should have been.
- A lesson the code no longer supports is `retired`. It stays in the file, marked, with
  why.
- An edit changes one entry. The file is never rewritten whole, since a rewrite drops what
  its writer did not think to keep.

The lessons are reconciled at each ship point, and whenever five have been added or changed
since the last pass: duplicates are merged, stale lessons are retired, scopes are checked,
and a lesson that can be stated without the target's names is proposed for the spec, as is
one a second campaign records again, by a proposal citing both. A lesson the pass changes
is `provisional` again.

## 6. Changes

#!/bin/bash
# run.sh <repo> <package> <cov dir>: build a coverage-instrumented scratch copy of the safe
# crate against the `coverage` variant, its test items under #[coverage(off)], and run each
# suite alone into <cov dir>/prof/<suite>: lib, each integration test binary, and doc. Each
# binary links the variant's C statically, so its profiles count the C and the Rust alike.
# report.py then reads the figures (testing spec, Coverage), with the variant's static archive
# as the C object.
set -euo pipefail
repo=$1 pkg=$2 out=$3
host=x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
nightly=$(sed -n 's/^nightly = "\(.*\)"$/\1/p' "$repo/Cargo.toml")
tree=$out/tree
rm -rf "$out"; mkdir -p "$tree/crustify" "$out/prof"
(cd "$repo" && tar -cf - --exclude=./target --exclude=./crustify --exclude=./c --exclude=./.git .) | (cd "$tree" && tar -xf -)
ln -s "$repo/c" "$tree/c"
ln -s "$repo/crustify/artifacts" "$tree/crustify/artifacts"
ln -s "$repo/crustify/builds" "$tree/crustify/builds"
python3 "$(dirname "$0")/mark.py" "$tree/src" "$tree/src/lib.rs"
cd "$tree"
export CRUSTIFY_BUILD_VARIANT=coverage CARGO_TARGET_DIR=$out/target
export RUSTFLAGS="-C instrument-coverage" RUSTDOCFLAGS="-C instrument-coverage -Z unstable-options --persist-doctests $out/doctests"
cargo "+$nightly" test -p "$pkg" --target $host --no-run --message-format=json 2>"$out/build.err" \
  | python3 -c 'import sys,json
for l in sys.stdin:
  try: d=json.loads(l)
  except: continue
  if d.get("reason")=="compiler-artifact" and d.get("executable") and d["target"]["kind"]!=["custom-build"] and d.get("profile",{}).get("test"): print(d["target"]["name"],d["target"]["kind"][0],d["executable"])' > "$out/bins.txt"
cat "$out/bins.txt"
while read -r name kind exe; do
  suite=$([ "$kind" = lib ] && echo lib || echo "$name")
  mkdir -p "$out/prof/$suite"
  echo "== $suite"
  LLVM_PROFILE_FILE="$out/prof/$suite/%p-%m.profraw" "$exe" --skip compile_fail > "$out/$suite.log" 2>&1 || echo "rc=$? in $suite"
  tail -3 "$out/$suite.log"
  "$exe" --list 2>/dev/null | grep -c ': test$' > "$out/$suite.count" || true
done < "$out/bins.txt"
mkdir -p "$out/prof/doc"
echo "== doc"
LLVM_PROFILE_FILE="$out/prof/doc/%p-%m.profraw" cargo "+$nightly" test -p "$pkg" --target $host --doc > "$out/doc.log" 2>&1 || echo "rc=$? in doc"
tail -3 "$out/doc.log"

# thread.c's equivalence tests at the switch

What `wave-226/batch-7/run-1`, the module pass, found of each equivalence test of
`src/util/thread.c` before the switch retires it. At the switch the raw bindings of the
twelve header functions and of the four `git_tlsdata_*` reach the module's exports, so each
of these tests would compare the Rust with itself: each retires, and none needs no C, so
none is carried over as it stands. Each row names the tests that outlive the C and keep what
it checks: the `unit_pub`, `ub_safe` and `ub_unsafe` tests, and the `unit_priv` tests of the
module's regions, the gateway's among them, which compile unconditionally from the switch on.

Whether they keep it was checked by seeding faults (`fault-seeding.md`, beside this file):
FAULTS_SUMMARY

## `tests/equiv/src/util/thread/atomics.rs`

| equivalence test | what it compares | kept by |
|---|---|---|
| `atomic32_sequences_match_the_c` | `Atomic32Ref`'s `get`, `set`, `inc`, `dec` and `add` against `git_atomic32_*`, step by step, from `0`, `1`, `-1`, `i32::MAX` and `i32::MIN`: returns and values | `unit_pub` `atomics::atomic32_operations_return_what_they_leave_and_wrap` and the five `atomics::atomic32_*` carried over from `threads/atomic.c`; `thread::arithmetic_wraps_at_the_bounds` |
| `atomic64_sequences_match_the_c` | the same for `Atomic64Ref`'s `get`, `set` and `add` against `git_atomic64_*` | `unit_pub` `atomics::atomic64_operations_return_what_they_leave_and_wrap`, `atomics::atomic_ssize_adds_and_reads_back` and the three `atomics::atomic64_*` |
| `pointer_slot_sequences_match_the_c` | `atomic_compare_and_swap`, `atomic_swap` and `atomic_load` over an `AtomicPtr` against `git_atomic__*` over a `void *` | `unit_pub` `atomics::cas_pointer`, `atomics::swap`, `atomics::load_ptr` and `atomics::a_compare_and_swap_to_the_same_value_succeeds` |
| `intptr_slot_sequences_match_the_c` | the same over an `intptr_t` slot, across the sign | `unit_pub` `atomics::cas_intptr`, `atomics::load_intptr` and `atomics::unsigned_slots_compare_swap_and_load` |
| `c_and_rust_share_one_count` | C's builtins and the port on one count from many threads: no update lost, each side reading the other's | `ub_safe` `atomics::a_refcount_rises_and_falls_from_many_threads` and `thread::shared_handles_add_from_many_threads`; the gateway's `unit_priv::exports_lose_no_update_across_threads`, which mixes the exports and the native API on one count. Sharing one object with C's builtins ends at the switch: no C builtin is left to share it with |
| `c_and_rust_race_to_install_one_value` | C's and the port's compare-and-swap racing to fill one slot | `ub_safe` `atomics::racing_initialisers_install_one_value` and `thread::compare_and_swap_from_many_threads` |

## `tests/equiv/src/util/thread/tlsdata.rs`

| equivalence test | what it compares | kept by |
|---|---|---|
| `set_get_and_dispose_match_c` | `test_threads_tlsdata__can_set_and_get`'s calls and more, on a POSIX key and a `TlsKey` | `unit_pub` `tlsdata::can_set_and_get` and `tlsdata::a_value_is_absent_until_stored_and_after_none`; the gateway's `unit_priv::the_exports_keep_cs_contract` for C's keys |
| `threads_match_c` | `test_threads_tlsdata__threads`'s ten threads | `unit_pub` `tlsdata::threads` and `tlsdata::a_static_key_serves_every_thread` |
| `destructors_run_on_the_values_c_destroys` | the values each destructor runs on at thread exit, after storing, replacing and removing, and none for a disposed key or a key without one | `unit_pub` `tlsdata::the_destructor_runs_at_thread_exit_on_the_values_held`, `tlsdata::set_returns_the_value_it_replaces_without_destroying_it`, `tlsdata::a_key_without_a_destructor_drops_its_values_at_thread_exit` and `tlsdata::a_disposed_key_names_no_key_and_destroys_nothing`; `ffi_import`'s `unit_priv::c_keys_store_words_and_destroy_them_at_thread_exit` for C's words and destructor |
| `refusals_of_a_key_naming_none_match_c` | the refusals of a key that names none | `unit_pub` `tlsdata::a_disposed_key_names_no_key_and_destroys_nothing` and `tlsdata::ids_are_never_reused`; the gateway's `unit_priv::key_zero_names_no_key` and `ffi_import`'s `unit_priv::c_reaches_no_rust_key_and_no_unknown_id` |

## The gateway's `equiv_priv` (`src/libgit2/src/util/thread.rs`, `mod ffi_export`)

These compare the exports with the header's `static inline` bodies, which the raw bindings
reach through `static_fns.c`'s `<name>__extern` wrappers until the switch removes the bodies
and the wrappers: the module goes, and with it the second implementation.

| equivalence test | kept by |
|---|---|
| `atomic32_exports_match_the_header` | `unit_priv::atomic32_exports_return_what_they_leave` |
| `atomic64_exports_match_the_header` | `unit_priv::atomic64_exports_return_what_they_leave` |
| `slot_exports_match_the_header` | `unit_priv::slot_exports_return_what_the_slot_held` and `unit_priv::slot_exports_carry_an_integer` |
| `exports_and_header_share_one_count` | `unit_priv::exports_lose_no_update_across_threads` |

After the switch the C that remains checks the exports too: the C suites `threads::atomic`,
`threads::tlsdata`, `threads::basic`, `threads::diff` and every suite that takes a reference
count, which the switch rehearsal of this run passed on `plain` (batch 6), ASan+UBSan and TSan.

content.content:
ffimap maps a Rust crate's FFI and unsafe surface deterministically: a rustc driver over
HIR and typeck counts unsafe blocks and fns, raw and void pointers by position and
visibility, FFI calls and wrapper use. No model is involved, so two runs over one tree
agree exactly. Its `--help` lists its flags, and its `docs/schema.md`, read in full before
its first scan, its counters and how a report combines them.

It counts what the build compiles of the safe crate itself, and prints one JSON document:

```bash
ffimap <workdir> > <file>.json
```

Every scan names the crate's seams, the functions that hand a value between its wrapper and
its raw form, so that each counter's `of_which.seam` share tells that plumbing apart from
the pointer management a consumer of the safe API faces: ffibox's handle seams `as_ptr`,
`as_mut_ptr`, `as_void_ptr`, `from_ptr` and `from_void_ptr`, the ownership hand-offs
`from_raw_parts`, `into_raw_parts`, `into_raw`, `from_c`, `into_c` and `as_c_ptr`, the adoption of a raw C
value, `from_raw`, and the view of a C object as another, `as_object`. A crate built on
ffibox is scanned with `--ffibox`, and its `-sys` crates are named with `--sys-crates`:

```bash
ffimap <workdir> --ffibox --sys-crates <the -sys crates> --regions ffi_import,ffi_export \
    --seams as_ptr,as_mut_ptr,as_void_ptr,from_ptr,from_void_ptr,from_raw_parts,into_raw_parts,into_raw,from_c,into_c,as_c_ptr,from_raw,as_object \
    > <file>.json
```

Raw bindings that are a module of the crate, not a crate of their own, laid out and
generated as [`bindgen`](../../rust/bindgen/SKILL.md) describes, are named to `--sys-crates`
by their path, `crate::<path>`, beside the `-sys` crates that remain. A named module joins
the inventory and leaves every other counter, as a `-sys` crate does. Left unnamed, its C
types and functions are in no inventory, the cells that read it are taken over the other
crates' alone, and the generated code counts as the crate's own, all with no error. A module
that holds hand-written code beside its declarations is left unnamed, since naming it would
take that code out of the scan.

In a port campaign, a scan names with `--features` the export feature of every module not
yet switched, as the [conventions](../../rust/conventions/SKILL.md)' Export features section
names them, so that the `ffi_export` gateways compiled under them are counted. Every scan
names the module's unsafe regions, as the conventions' Unsafe regions section names them,
with `--regions`.

Two scans are compared only when they name the same seams, regions and features.

Its counters form one tree, each named by its dotted path into the scan's `counts`, as
ffimap's `docs/schema.md` describes; a metric is a counter, or a combination of counters
that schema allows: a partition's leaves summed, a share read against the record it cuts,
or subtracted from it. `--sites <counter> ...` also lists where each named counter's
increments are, and takes leaves only, such as `fn.unsafe.pub`; the workspace is named
before it. The counters that recur:

content.content:
## Safety audit

Deterministic `ffimap`, run as the `ffimap` skill's Accounting section describes; no
model. Every counter is in the `ffimap.json` tracked in the campaign's artifact dir, in
each wave's `waves/wave-<index>/` and in each batch run's dir. Each metric is one counter
or a combination of counters, named by their dotted paths into the scan's `counts`; a `%`
metric is a share within one record, and a `−` subtracts a share from the record it cuts.

### Metrics

| metric | counters | what it counts |
|---|---|---|
| pub raw ptr | `raw_ptr.total.safe.pub` | raw pointers a consumer meets without writing `unsafe`: public fields and the signatures of safe public fns; target 0 |
| pub void ptr | `raw_ptr.field.of_which.void.pub` + `raw_ptr.fn_sig_arg.of_which.void.{safe,unsafe}.pub` + `raw_ptr.fn_sig_ret.of_which.void.{safe,unsafe}.pub` | type-erased pointers left to the API's users, `unsafe fn`s included |
| pub unsafe fn | `fn.unsafe.pub` | the obligations the crate exports to its callers |
| &cell | `ty.ffibox.wrapper.as.borrowed.std.pub` − `….of_which.self_in_ref_accessor.pub` − `….of_which.self_in_trait_impl.pub` | public references to a cell outside the positions ffibox sanctions, where the convention wants a handle; target 0 |
| C by value | `ty.ffibox.sys.as.by_val.total` + `ty.ffibox.sys.as.owned.std.total` | C structs held by value or in a standard-library owner rather than through a cell, which a move can leave dangling |
| celled % | `ty.ffibox.sys.of_which.raw_ptr_in_sys.of_which.wrapped` / `….of_which.used` | of the C types the bindings pass by pointer that the crate uses, those a cell covers |
| raw→std | `raw_ptr.casted_to.std.total` | raw pointers turned into a standard-library borrow, slice, string or owner, whose lifetime or ownership the type system then trusts |
| unmanaged ptr types | `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.none.total` | types that store a raw pointer and declare nothing about it |
| ptr Drop | `ty.storing_raw_ptr.of_which.impl_drop.total` | types that store a raw pointer and free it by hand, rather than through an owner |
| Send/Sync | `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.send.total` + `ty.impl_trait.of_which.std.sync.total` | thread safety asserted rather than derived from the fields |
| raw deref | `raw_ptr.deref.total` | raw-pointer reads and writes in bodies, each a pointer the code vouches for |
| FFI calls | `code.unsafe_call.ffi` | calls across the C boundary, through bindings or stored function pointers |
| unsafe loc % | `code.loc.unsafe` / `code.loc.total` | lines of unsafe code over code lines; the comparable measure of unsafe volume |
| unsafe blocks | `code.unsafe_block.total` − `code.unsafe_block.of_which.ffi_export` | hand-written unsafe blocks, a port's generated export gateways left out; moves with the one-op-per-block policy, so not comparable across crates |

## Planning

# A port batch runs its module's tests with its exports linked in place of its C

Status: `open`.

## Signal

One procedure repeated by hand, which no gate runs. `testing-gates`' Regressions section
has a `port` batch check and lint the safe crate with its module's export feature on,
"which compiles the module's gateway without linking it", and compare each export's
signature with its raw binding. Nothing runs the gateway before the module's switch: every
gate builds with the feature off, and the `testing` skill puts an export's tests "with the
stage that removes the form", which compile only under the feature. A gateway that
compiles, and has C's signature, but writes the wrong out-parameter, reads past its size or
mishandles a NULL, passes every gate until the switch rebuilds the variants, when the C
tests that remain are the first to call it.

## Evidence

- `wave-229/batch-0/run-1` (`src/util/utf8.c`, the crate's first gateway) ran, "as a
  scratch check, not a gate", its tests with the exports linked in place of the archive's
  `utf8.o` (its dashboard notes).
- `wave-229/batch-1/run-1`, its module pass, did it again, by hand: a private build dir under
  `crustify/tmp/` whose entries link to the variant's, but for a copy of its static archive
  without the module's objects (`ar d libcrustify.a utf8.c.o`), named by
  `CRUSTIFY_BUILD_DIR`; then `cargo-variant.sh <variant> test --workspace --features
  ffi-export-src-util-utf8-c` on `plain` and `asan-ubsan`, which passed but for the known
  nightly failures, `nm` showing no `utf8proc_utf8class` and `next_hfs_char` calling Rust.
  It also relinked the variant's C test executables (`libgit2_tests`, `util_tests`) from
  their `build.ninja` edges, without `src/util/CMakeFiles/util.dir/utf8.c.o` and with the
  crate built as a `staticlib` with the feature on: `-sutf8`, and `-spath -sdiff -sindex
  -scheckout -srefs`, gave the stock binaries' results (825 passed, 22 skipped). A
  `util_tests` input list holds two `utf8.c.o`, the module's and its C test's, so removing
  by file name alone would drop the test: the procedure must name the object's path.
- The module pass added the gateway's own `unit_priv` tests, which compile only under the
  feature, and ran them by hand with it on, under Miri too.
- `wave-186/batch-5/run-1` and `wave-186/batch-6/run-1` (`git2/src/cli/opt.c`) ran the
  module's `equiv` tests the same way, by hand, against a copy of the archive without
  `opt.c.o`; those tests compare the C with the Rust, so with the exports linked they compare
  the exports with the native API, and they are retired with the C at the switch.
- `wave-186/batch-7/run-1`, the module pass, found the gateway with no test of its own and two
  defects that only the export's callers reach. Its gateway tests, written after `main.c`,
  `cmd_hash_object.c` and `common.c`, ran with the feature on against the private build and
  under Miri, where the feature also compiles: Miri reported
  `ub_export/args-slot-handed-to-c-through-a-dead-borrow`, a `char **` the export stored for C
  that a later unique reborrow invalidated, which no gate could reach, since every gate builds
  with the feature off. The module's remaining C is an executable, the CLI, which no C test
  runs (`modules.json`'s `tests` is empty, and no suite under `c/tests` reaches `src/cli`), so
  the switch's C-test gate checks nothing of these exports. The pass relinked the variant's
  `git2` from its `build.ninja` edge, without `src/cli/CMakeFiles/git2_cli.dir/opt.c.o` and
  with the crate built as a `staticlib` with the feature on, and ran it and the stock `git2`
  over 66 command lines in scratch repositories: 62 alike, the 4 others the parser's recorded
  departures from the C. The procedure is recorded for this target as a lesson
  (`crustify/LESSONS.md`, "A `git2` module's exports are checked through the CLI").

- `wave-194/batch-4/run-1` (`deps/llhttp/api.c`, its last `port` batch) ran it by hand again,
  as its task message asked, on `plain` and `asan-ubsan`: private build dirs under
  `crustify/tmp/linkcheck/<variant>` linking to the variant's entries, with a copy of
  `libcrustify.a` less `api.c.o` (211 objects), named by `CRUSTIFY_BUILD_DIR`, and the tests
  run with `--features ffi-export-deps-llhttp-api-c`. Two things the procedure must say came
  out of it. First, not every test binary can link: the module's `equiv` binary calls 19 of
  api.c's functions that no remaining C calls and that therefore have no export
  (`llhttp_get_type`, the lenient setters, `llhttp_reset`, …), so it fails to link
  (`undefined symbol`), by design, since it compares with that C; the check runs the other
  binaries and the doctests, and the undefined symbols of `equiv` are the list of the module's
  unexported functions, every one of which should be api.c's own. Second, a test outside
  `equiv` that calls such a function through its raw binding fails to link too, and would
  fail at the switch: `ub_unsafe`'s llhttp fixtures called `llhttp_settings_init`, which the
  batch replaced with the zeroed table it makes. The rest passed (`lib` 858 with the gateway's
  six tests, `ub_safe` 785, `ub_unsafe` 134, `unit_pub` 156, doctests 92 and 387; under
  ASan+UBSan the same but for the known nightly `compile_fail` snapshots and `CommitBuilder`
  doctest), `nm` showing the exports defined and api.c's other symbols absent.

- `wave-194/batch-7/run-1`, api.c's module pass, found that leaving `equiv` out of the check
  is itself a gap. `equiv` is one binary for every module, and `llhttp.c`'s equivalence
  tests (`tests/equiv/deps/llhttp/llhttp.rs`), which stay, also called 10 of api.c's
  unexported functions, so retiring api.c's own equivalence file at the switch would still
  have left `equiv` unlinked
  (`misc/llhttp-equiv-tests-call-api-c-functions-without-exports`). `rust-lld` lists only
  20 undefined symbols by default, so the full list needs its `--error-limit=0`. The
  pass moved those tests into api.c's file, then ran the check over a scratch tree with that
  file retired, as the switch will: `equiv` linked, 532 passing on `plain`, ASan+UBSan and
  TSan. So the check must link `equiv` too, with only the module's own equivalence files
  retired, and fail on any undefined symbol it references from another module's file.

- `wave-197/batch-0/run-1` (`deps/llhttp/http.c`, its whole `port`) ran the check by hand
  again, as its task message asked, on `plain` and `asan-ubsan`, over a scratch tree with its
  own equivalence file retired: every binary linked, `equiv` included (532), and passed but
  for the known nightly failures under ASan+UBSan. Removing the module's object by name would
  have removed the wrong one: the archive holds two `http.c.o` members,
  `src/libgit2/transports/http.c`'s (the 154th) and `deps/llhttp/http.c`'s (the 168th), and

# A port batch runs its module's tests with its exports linked in place of its C

Status: `open`.

## Signal

One procedure repeated by hand, which no gate runs. `testing-gates`' Regressions section
has a `port` batch check and lint the safe crate with its module's export feature on,
"which compiles the module's gateway without linking it", and compare each export's
signature with its raw binding. Nothing runs the gateway before the module's switch: every
gate builds with the feature off, and the `testing` skill puts an export's tests "with the
stage that removes the form", which compile only under the feature. A gateway that
compiles, and has C's signature, but writes the wrong out-parameter, reads past its size or
mishandles a NULL, passes every gate until the switch rebuilds the variants, when the C
tests that remain are the first to call it.

## Evidence

- `wave-229/batch-0/run-1` (`src/util/utf8.c`, the crate's first gateway) ran, "as a
  scratch check, not a gate", its tests with the exports linked in place of the archive's
  `utf8.o` (its dashboard notes).
- `wave-229/batch-1/run-1`, its module pass, did it again, by hand: a private build dir under
  `crustify/tmp/` whose entries link to the variant's, but for a copy of its static archive
  without the module's objects (`ar d libcrustify.a utf8.c.o`), named by
  `CRUSTIFY_BUILD_DIR`; then `cargo-variant.sh <variant> test --workspace --features
  ffi-export-src-util-utf8-c` on `plain` and `asan-ubsan`, which passed but for the known
  nightly failures, `nm` showing no `utf8proc_utf8class` and `next_hfs_char` calling Rust.
  It also relinked the variant's C test executables (`libgit2_tests`, `util_tests`) from
  their `build.ninja` edges, without `src/util/CMakeFiles/util.dir/utf8.c.o` and with the
  crate built as a `staticlib` with the feature on: `-sutf8`, and `-spath -sdiff -sindex
  -scheckout -srefs`, gave the stock binaries' results (825 passed, 22 skipped). A
  `util_tests` input list holds two `utf8.c.o`, the module's and its C test's, so removing
  by file name alone would drop the test: the procedure must name the object's path.
- The module pass added the gateway's own `unit_priv` tests, which compile only under the
  feature, and ran them by hand with it on, under Miri too.
- `wave-186/batch-5/run-1` and `wave-186/batch-6/run-1` (`git2/src/cli/opt.c`) ran the
  module's `equiv` tests the same way, by hand, against a copy of the archive without
  `opt.c.o`; those tests compare the C with the Rust, so with the exports linked they compare
  the exports with the native API, and they are retired with the C at the switch.
- `wave-186/batch-7/run-1`, the module pass, found the gateway with no test of its own and two
  defects that only the export's callers reach. Its gateway tests, written after `main.c`,
  `cmd_hash_object.c` and `common.c`, ran with the feature on against the private build and
  under Miri, where the feature also compiles: Miri reported
  `ub_export/args-slot-handed-to-c-through-a-dead-borrow`, a `char **` the export stored for C
  that a later unique reborrow invalidated, which no gate could reach, since every gate builds
  with the feature off. The module's remaining C is an executable, the CLI, which no C test
  runs (`modules.json`'s `tests` is empty, and no suite under `c/tests` reaches `src/cli`), so
  the switch's C-test gate checks nothing of these exports. The pass relinked the variant's
  `git2` from its `build.ninja` edge, without `src/cli/CMakeFiles/git2_cli.dir/opt.c.o` and
  with the crate built as a `staticlib` with the feature on, and ran it and the stock `git2`
  over 66 command lines in scratch repositories: 62 alike, the 4 others the parser's recorded
  departures from the C. The procedure is recorded for this target as a lesson
  (`crustify/LESSONS.md`, "A `git2` module's exports are checked through the CLI").

- `wave-194/batch-4/run-1` (`deps/llhttp/api.c`, its last `port` batch) ran it by hand again,
  as its task message asked, on `plain` and `asan-ubsan`: private build dirs under
  `crustify/tmp/linkcheck/<variant>` linking to the variant's entries, with a copy of
  `libcrustify.a` less `api.c.o` (211 objects), named by `CRUSTIFY_BUILD_DIR`, and the tests
  run with `--features ffi-export-deps-llhttp-api-c`. Two things the procedure must say came
  out of it. First, not every test binary can link: the module's `equiv` binary calls 19 of
  api.c's functions that no remaining C calls and that therefore have no export
  (`llhttp_get_type`, the lenient setters, `llhttp_reset`, …), so it fails to link
  (`undefined symbol`), by design, since it compares with that C; the check runs the other
  binaries and the doctests, and the undefined symbols of `equiv` are the list of the module's
  unexported functions, every one of which should be api.c's own. Second, a test outside
  `equiv` that calls such a function through its raw binding fails to link too, and would
  fail at the switch: `ub_unsafe`'s llhttp fixtures called `llhttp_settings_init`, which the
  batch replaced with the zeroed table it makes. The rest passed (`lib` 858 with the gateway's
  six tests, `ub_safe` 785, `ub_unsafe` 134, `unit_pub` 156, doctests 92 and 387; under
  ASan+UBSan the same but for the known nightly `compile_fail` snapshots and `CommitBuilder`
  doctest), `nm` showing the exports defined and api.c's other symbols absent.

- `wave-194/batch-7/run-1`, api.c's module pass, found that leaving `equiv` out of the check
  is itself a gap. `equiv` is one binary for every module, and `llhttp.c`'s equivalence
  tests (`tests/equiv/deps/llhttp/llhttp.rs`), which stay, also called 10 of api.c's
  unexported functions, so retiring api.c's own equivalence file at the switch would still
  have left `equiv` unlinked
  (`misc/llhttp-equiv-tests-call-api-c-functions-without-exports`). `rust-lld` lists only
  20 undefined symbols by default, so the full list needs its `--error-limit=0`. The
  pass moved those tests into api.c's file, then ran the check over a scratch tree with that
  file retired, as the switch will: `equiv` linked, 532 passing on `plain`, ASan+UBSan and
  TSan. So the check must link `equiv` too, with only the module's own equivalence files
  retired, and fail on any undefined symbol it references from another module's file.

- `wave-197/batch-0/run-1` (`deps/llhttp/http.c`, its whole `port`) ran the check by hand
  again, as its task message asked, on `plain` and `asan-ubsan`, over a scratch tree with its
  own equivalence file retired: every binary linked, `equiv` included (532), and passed but
  for the known nightly failures under ASan+UBSan. Removing the module's object by name would
  have removed the wrong one: the archive holds two `http.c.o` members,
  `src/libgit2/transports/http.c`'s (the 154th) and `deps/llhttp/http.c`'s (the 168th), and
  `ar d libcrustify.a http.c.o` deletes the first; the batch used `ar dN 2` and checked with
  `nm` that the member left defines `git_smart_subtransport_http`. So the script must take
  the module's objects by their `build.ninja` paths, as the `util_tests` evidence above found
  for a link's inputs, and pick an archive member by position, never by its base name alone.
  It also relinked the variants' `git2` and `libgit2_tests` from their `build.ninja` edges,
  without `deps/llhttp/CMakeFiles/llhttp.dir/http.c.o` and with the crate's static library
  built with the feature on, and ran `crustify/scripts/http-gate.sh` over them on `plain`,
  `asan-ubsan` and `coverage`, the module's only C callers being the HTTP client and
  `llhttp.c`, which no offline C test reaches.

- `wave-226/batch-3/run-1` (`src/util/thread.c`'s thread-local storage) ran the check by
  hand, as a scratch run, not a gate: the whole workspace built with
  `ffi-export-src-util-thread-c` on, on `plain`, links the four `git_tlsdata_*` exports in
  place of the archive's `thread.c.o`, whose only definitions they are, so that the member
  is never pulled and no duplicate symbol is reported. Every binary passed (`lib` 914, the
  gateway's own two tests among them, `equiv` 535, `ub_safe` 808, `ub_unsafe` 148,
  `unit_pub` 266, doctests 111 and 400), with `errors.c`'s and `oid.c`'s keys on the Rust
  registry. No C test binary was relinked.

## Destination

The spec: `testing-gates`' Regressions section, the export checks of a `port` batch, with a
script beside it, as `authoring` places a procedure that must run exactly so, documented by
its `--help`: given a variant and the module's objects, as `build.ninja` names them, it
makes the private build dir with an archive lacking them, runs the workspace's tests with
the module's export feature on against it, and, where the target builds C test
executables, relinks them against the crate's static library in place of the module's
objects and runs the suites tied to the module and to the modules that call its exports.

The script also runs the gateway's own tests under Miri with the export feature on, which
Miri's builds allow before the switch since they link no C, and, where the module's remaining
C callers are executables that no C test runs, names that check as the gap it is: an export
whose only C callers are executables is checked by its gateway tests alone, which `testing`'s
UB tests section would have written after those callers, or by a relink of the executables
compared with the stock ones over the inputs the target documents.

## Change

Not made: a script and a new gate want their own review, and the module's integration,
right after this pass, exercises the same link through the target's build system. The
section would say that a `port` batch, and its module pass, run the check on `plain` and
`asan-ubsan`, and that a module's switch still runs the C tests over the actual build.

## Validation

To be run: the script on `wave-229`'s tree, passing, and failing when the gateway's
`bytes()` reads one byte past `str_len` (which the module pass's tests catch under Miri) or
when `git_utf8_iterate` leaves `*out` unwritten on a refusal.

## Review

Pending.

# Faults seeded in thread.c before the switch

What `wave-226/batch-7/run-1`, the module pass, seeded in `src/libgit2/src/util/thread.rs`
before the switch retires the module's equivalence tests, as `ubc_check.c`'s module pass did
(`module-pass-seeds-faults-before-the-switch`, on `crustify/devel`): one fault at a time, each
one site changed, the module's tests run over each, binary by binary.

## How

`fault-seeding/`, beside this record, holds the run:

- `mutants.py <thread.rs> <mutants.json>` writes the 64 faults, each an exact replacement of
  one site: a returned value (the one found where the one left is due, a flipped bit), a
  constant (`+ 1`, `^ 1`, the first id), an operator (add for subtract, saturating for
  wrapping), a comparison (a check dropped, `all` for `any`) or a statement dropped. Each site
  is checked unique in the file.
- `mutate.py <scratch tree> <mutants.json> <results.json> [ids…]` applies each fault to a
  scratch copy of the tree (`git archive HEAD`, `c/` and `crustify/builds` linked), builds
  with `ffi-export-src-util-thread-c` on, as the switch compiles the gateway, and runs
  `cargo-variant.sh plain test --features ffi-export-src-util-thread-c <binary> --
  util::thread` for `lib`, `unit_pub`, `ub_safe`, `ub_unsafe` and `equiv`, each under a
  240 s timeout; a failed test, or a binary that times out or ends without a result, catches
  the fault.
- `classify.py <results.json>` tallies them: the equivalence tests are the `equiv` binary's
  and the gateway's `equiv_priv`; every other test outlives the C.

`results-before.json` is the run over the wave's tip (`2f2ffb73d`); `results-after.json`
reruns, over this pass's tree, the three faults no test caught.

## What it found

| region | faults | outliving tests catch, at the tip | after this pass | equivalence tests catch |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| native atomics (`Atomic32Ref`, `Atomic64Ref`, `AtomicWord`) | 21 | 20 | 20 | 20 |
| the gateway (`mod ffi_export`) | 18 | 18 | 18 | 17 |
| thread-local storage (`tls`, `TlsKey`) | 19 | 17 | 19 | 9 |
| locks | 3 | 3 | 3 | 0 |
| threads (`ThreadRef`, `ThreadMut`, `JoinHandle`) | 3 | 3 | 3 | 0 |
| **all** | **64** | **61** | **63** | **46** |

- No fault is caught by the equivalence tests alone: what they check, the tests that stay
  check too, as `equiv-retirement.md` maps test by test.
- The one fault nothing catches, `load-cas`, makes `load` write back the value it read with a
  swap; it returns the same value and leaves the same value, so it is equivalent: no test,
  of either kind, can tell it apart.
- Two faults of the thread-local storage escaped every test at the tip, and this pass added a
  test for each, which catches it:
  - `t-prune-any`, a prune that stops when any entry of the thread's table is live, leaves a
    disposed key's entry beside a live key's, and the next store under the disposed key
    replaces it and succeeds. `unit_pub`'s
    `tlsdata::a_key_disposed_beside_a_live_one_names_no_key` stores under two keys, disposes
    of one and checks that a store under it fails and its values are dropped.
  - `t-first-store-any`, a thread's first store under an id that ignores the key's kind, lets
    C store a word under a Rust key's id. `ffi_import`'s
    `unit_priv::c_reaches_no_rust_key_from_a_thread_that_holds_none` makes the store from a
    thread that holds no value of the key; the existing test made it from one that did, where
    the entry's kind refused it.
- 16 of the 18 faults of the gateway are caught only by the gateway's own `unit_priv` tests,
  which compile only under the module's export feature and so run in no gate before the
  switch; from the switch on they run in every one. The other two (`x-set-null`,
  `x-get-null`) are also caught by `unit_pub`'s `sync::each_thread_sets_its_own_error`, whose
  error state is C's `errors.c` on the exports.

## Each fault

FAULT_TABLE

What `wave-226/batch-7/run-1`, the module pass, ran under `crustify/tmp/`, beside
`wave-226/batch-6/run-1`'s rehearsal on `plain` (its `switch-rehearsal.md`), whose step 1 it
repeats. Nothing was committed to `c/`, and the scratch was deleted after the run.

   with the fork's `.git` (`git clone --shared` of the worktree's `c/`; a `git archive` alone
   fails `perf::merge` and skips three cases, `crustify/LESSONS.md`'s
   `switch-rehearsal-c-is-a-git-checkout`). `src/util/thread.c` is removed, and the twelve
   `GIT_INLINE` definitions of `thread.h` and `unix/pthread.h` are replaced by batch 6's
   prototypes, by the script `switch-headers.py`'s edit: in `thread.h`, the `GIT_THREADS`
   branch from `git_atomic32_set`'s comment to the `#else` of the build without threads
   becomes the eleven `extern` prototypes; in `unix/pthread.h`,
   `GIT_INLINE(int) git_threads_global_init(void) { return 0; }` becomes
   `extern int git_threads_global_init(void);`.
2. The copy's `crustify/scripts/rust-staticlib.sh` builds with
   `--features bindgen,ffi-export-src-util-thread-c`. `asan-ubsan` and `tsan` were configured
   and built from `build.json`'s commands (version 7) in build dirs of the copy, with
   `CRUSTIFY_BINDINGS_UPDATE=1`. Both `libcrustify.a` hold 208 objects, `thread.c.o` gone;
   both `libgit2_tests` define `git_atomic32_inc`, `git_threads_global_init` and
   `git_tlsdata_get` from the Rust library, and no `<name>__extern` wrapper of the module.
3. `crustify/scripts/c-tests.sh` over each, 16 suites side by side:

   | variant | passed | failed | skipped | non-zero suites | baseline |
   |---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
   | `asan-ubsan` | 3442 | 0 | 55 | none | matches |
   | `tsan` | 3442 | 0 | 55 | the baseline's 10 | matches |

   Under TSan, `threads::diff` and `threads::refdb` exit 66, as in the baseline, each with one
   report and no Rust frame: `filter.c`'s lazy `filter_initialize` and glibc's `tzset`. The
   module's tied suites, on both: `threads::atomic` 13, `threads::basic` 4,
   `threads::tlsdata` 2, `threads::diff` 2, `threads::refdb` 1, `pack::sharing` 1,
   `pack::threadsafety` 1, `repo::getters` 5, `repo::setters` 5 and `util_tests`' `init` 3,
   all passing. Under ASan+UBSan, LeakSanitizer finds nothing: the error states that
   `threads::basic::set_error`'s C threads allocate are freed at their exit by the Rust
   registry's thread-local destructor, as POSIX's key destructor freed them.

So the switch, as batch 6 recorded it, leaves the C tests at the baseline on `plain`,
`asan-ubsan` and `tsan`. Not rehearsed: `coverage`, `bsan` and the packaging gate.

"""report.py <cov dir> <name>=<dir>[:<dir>...][@<compilation dir>],... --c <C object>...

Merges each suite's profiles under <cov dir>/prof/, the four suites' union as TOTAL and every
suite's as ALL, and prints the TOTAL line of `llvm-cov report` for each named scope, with the C
objects and every test and doctest binary as objects for every suite. A scope's @<dir>
resolves the relative paths a C build recorded. MERGED=1 reuses the merged profiles, and ONLY=<suite> reports that one alone.

A scope written `<name>=@c`, such as `C=@c`, reads the C objects alone, with no source filter:
the archive holds only the link unit's TUs, whatever paths their build recorded. Any other
scope fails when a file it reports lies outside its dirs: llvm-cov falls back to every object
when its filters match no source, which would count the test binaries' std and Rust as C.

The C objects are those of the coverage variant's static archive, its `static` in build.json
(crustify/builds/coverage/crustify/libcrustify.a), which the test binaries link: each binary holds
only the TUs it reaches, so the archive, which llvm-cov reads member by member, gives every TU
its place in the denominator, one no test reaches at zero."""
import subprocess,sys,pathlib,json,glob,os
out0=pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1])
nightly=os.environ.get("NIGHTLY") or next(l.split('"')[1] for l in open(out0/"tree"/"Cargo.toml") if l.startswith("nightly = "))
sysroot=subprocess.run(['rustc','+'+nightly,'--print','sysroot'],capture_output=True,text=True,check=True).stdout.strip()
B=sysroot+'/lib/rustlib/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/bin/'
out=pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]); scopes=dict(s.split('=',1) for s in sys.argv[2].split(','))
cobjs=sys.argv[sys.argv.index('--c')+1:]
bins=[l.split()[2] for l in (out/'bins.txt').read_text().splitlines()]
docs=[p for p in glob.glob(str(out/'doctests'/'**'/'rust_out'),recursive=True)]
objs=cobjs+bins+docs
suites=sorted(p.name for p in (out/'prof').iterdir() if any(p.glob('*.profraw')))
def merge(name,dirs):
    raws=[str(r) for d in dirs for r in (out/'prof'/d).glob('*.profraw')]
    prof=out/f'{name}.profdata'
    subprocess.run([B+'llvm-profdata','merge','-sparse','-o',str(prof)]+raws,check=True)
    return prof
def total(prof,srcs):
    cd=[]
    if srcs==['@c']: use,srcs=cobjs,[]
    else:
        use=objs
        if '@' in srcs[-1]: srcs[-1],c=srcs[-1].split('@'); cd=['-compilation-dir='+c]
    args=[B+'llvm-cov','report','-instr-profile',str(prof)]+cd+[use[0]]+sum((['-object',o] for o in use[1:]),[])+srcs
    r=subprocess.run(args,capture_output=True,text=True)

### `libgit2/src/util/thread.c` wave 226 batch 7: module pass

The module pass over the module's 13 paths, for every objective with `fix`, and the only
review of batch 6 (`2f2ffb73d`), the exports of the twelve `static inline` functions of
`thread.h` and `unix/pthread.h`. It files no finding. Batch 5's four reports and batch 4's
two were not revisited: none is a `ub`, `equiv` or `logic` defect that still reproduces, and
their fixes are in the tree. No lesson was `provisional`.

The gateway was reviewed for what the C that stays relies on from the switch on: every
reference count, `errors.c`'s `threadstate_get` and `git_libgit2_init`'s `init_fns`. Each
atomic export is the one sequentially consistent operation the builtin is, over the caller's
object, with C's wrapping; it forms no reference to the C struct (`CRefSeam::from_ptr` builds
the handle from the pointer alone, and `val` lends an `&AtomicI32` over the field), so other
threads' atomic writes, C's or Rust's, race nothing. That `ref_from_ptr`'s text does not yet
admit those writes is `ffibox-atomic-layout-types`'s, which batch 6 recorded. On a null
object each export aborts, where the builtin would fault; no C caller passes one. The thread-
local exports take no lock on a read, a replacement or a thread's exit, run C's destructor on
the values a C thread still holds at its exit, `pthread_exit` included, and report a store
made while the thread exits, or under a key that names none, as -1, which `errors.c` and
`oid.c` ignore at the cost of the value's leak, as with POSIX's. The forked child of
`git_process_start` sets no error before `exit`, so it never takes the registry's lock.

The switch was rehearsed again on `asan-ubsan` and `tsan` (batch 6 rehearsed `plain`), from a
copy of the tip with `thread.c` removed and batch 6's prototypes in place, the crate's static
library built with the feature: `c-tests.sh` matched the baseline on both, 3442 passed, 0
failed, 55 skipped, LeakSanitizer and the module's tied suites included (the run dir's
`switch-rehearsal.md`). With the feature on, the workspace passes on `plain`, ASan+UBSan and
TSan, libgit2's C error state on the Rust registry in every test binary, and the gateway's
tests under Miri. No C test leaves at the switch: the tied cases each call the module through
the macros its headers keep, through the exports, or read `git_atomic32.val`, whose layout the
header keeps.

Before the equivalence tests retire, 64 faults were seeded in `thread.rs`, one site each
(`fault-seeding.md`): the tests that outlive the C caught 61 on the tip, the equivalence tests
46, none that the others missed; the one nothing catches is equivalent. The two that escaped
are thread-local storage's, a prune that stops at the first live entry and a first store that
ignores the key's kind, and the pass adds a test for each (`test-adequacy`):
`unit_pub`'s `tlsdata::a_key_disposed_beside_a_live_one_names_no_key` and `ffi_import`'s
`unit_priv::c_reaches_no_rust_key_from_a_thread_that_holds_none`, which bring it to 63. The
gateway gains `unit_priv::the_atomic_exports_abort_on_a_null_object`, compiled under the
feature until the switch: each of the eleven atomic exports, given a null object in a forked
child, ends it with `SIGABRT`. `equiv-retirement.md` maps each of the 14 equivalence tests
to the tests that keep what it checks.

Gates, on the wave's tip before any change and on the landed tree, against gen5: format;
`clippy --workspace --all-targets` with warnings denied, the feature off and on; the
workspace on `plain`, ASan+UBSan and TSan; Miri per test binary. BSan ran over the three
added tests alone, with no report; at a wave's end it runs only at a ship point from
2026-11-15, the user's departure. The slow list holds no test of these stages.
